clue.text: An advisory group sailing?

parts.note: a board is a group that gives advice or directs, like a board of governors

explanation.surface: A committee of advisers is out on a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a pun: 'aboard' means on a ship, so a board out on the water is sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship that is under way means you are sailing.

clue.text: Frame for those climbing out of bed?

definitions.text: Frame for those climbing out of bed?

parts.words: Frame for those climbing out of bed?
parts.note: reads like a support for people getting up in the morning; really a garden frame for climbing plants growing up out of the flower bed

explanation.surface: A grab rail to help sleepy people get up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood fixed to a wall supports climbing plants like roses that grow from the garden border.

clue.text: Sections of personal columns

parts.note: sounds like parts of a newspaper's personal ads; really the bones of each person's spinal column

explanation.surface: Parts of the personal ads page in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is made of separate bones stacked one on another, the units of everyone's own backbone.

clue.text: He becomes an aircrew member automatically

definitions.text: He becomes an aircrew member automatically

parts.words: He becomes an aircrew member automatically
parts.note: reads as a man drafted onto a flight crew; really the RAF slang name for an aircraft's automatic pilot

explanation.surface: A man is enrolled in a flight crew without any choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilots of the RAF nicknamed the autopilot 'George', so he joins the crew whenever the plane flies itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The autopilot was given a man's name by airmen, as if it were another crew member flying the plane.

clue.text: When this cover is on the joint it's a gander!

definitions.text: When this cover is on the joint it's a gander!

parts.words: When this cover is on the joint it's a gander!
parts.note: a ... covers a joint in pipework, but '... the joint' is slang for taking a look (a gander) at a place before robbing it

explanation.surface: A plumber notes that a pipe joint gets a protective sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is slang for a look, and 'casing the joint' is criminal slang for inspecting premises before a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering or sheath is a case around something, and the word also means reconnoitring a place.

clue.text: Agitated demoniac laughter he causes

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up or shaken, so the letters of the next word are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A frenzied demon-possessed man makes people laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' shakes up DEMONIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up entertainer is someone whose job is to make audiences laugh.

clue.text: Chaps bent on serving stand offish sorts?

definitions.text: Chaps bent on serving stand offish sorts?

parts.words: Chaps bent on serving stand offish sorts?
parts.note: seems to describe men keen to wait on aloof people; really rugby forwards bent over, whose ball is fed out to the stand-off half

explanation.surface: Men determined to wait on snooty, aloof people.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the 'stand-off' (fly-half) receives the ball once it comes out of the pack of bent-over forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the forwards bind together, heads down, to contest the ball, which then goes out to the backs.

clue.text: Roughly patching evening wear

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters of the next word are set down loosely in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mending an evening outfit in a slapdash way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges PATCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft cap was traditionally worn in bed, so it is clothing put on for the night.

clue.text: One of the soldiers on the march?

definitions.text: One of the soldiers on the march?

parts.words: One of the soldiers on the march?
parts.note: seems to be a marching soldier; really a soldier from the King's Own Scottish ..., or anyone living on the Marches, the border lands

explanation.surface: A soldier parading with his regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches are the border lands between England and Scotland or Wales; the King's Own Scottish Borderers was a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living near a frontier, or a soldier of a border regiment, lives in the Marches.

clue.text: Shade, for example, put back? There's resentment here

parts.note: the umbra is the darkest part of a shadow

indicators.note: put back means the abbreviation is placed in reverse order

explanation.surface: A tree's shadow, moved elsewhere, upsets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like the definition but is the wordplay; the definition is 'resentment' at the other end. 'put back' reverses the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence or feeling a grievance is the sense of taking umbrage.

clue.text: Distribute shares-a good deal, we hear!

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be said out loud and spelt as another word

parts.note: a good deal means a lot, a large amount

explanation.surface: Handing out stock makes a profitable bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns the spoken 'a lot' into the written ALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or hand out portions is to give each person their share.

clue.text: His heroine could not stand winning

definitions.text: His heroine could not stand winning

parts.words: His heroine could not stand winning
parts.note: seems to be a sore winner; really Kate Hardcastle in the play 'She Stoops to Conquer', who stoops rather than stands to win

explanation.surface: A man's leading lady was a graceless victor.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith wrote 'She Stoops to Conquer': his heroine stoops, so she does not stand, to conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright wrote the comedy whose heroine stoops to conquer.

clue.text: Yellow and black sphere

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A ball coloured yellow and black like a wasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe or ball, such as the jewelled royal one, is a round body.

clue.text: Forward perhaps but not one to make passes usually

definitions.text: Forward perhaps but not one to make passes usually

parts.words: Forward perhaps but not one to make passes usually
parts.note: reads like a bold person who still does not flirt; really a footballer who runs with the ball at his feet instead of passing it

explanation.surface: A bold person who nonetheless rarely flirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a pushy suitor and 'passes' romantic advances; in football a forward who keeps the ball rather than passing it runs with it at his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who runs the ball forward at close control instead of passing it is said to dribble.

clue.text: Star, exploding, takes a year to get off-course…

indicators.note: exploding blows the word apart, so its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A supernova that takes a year to blow apart drifts away.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 17-across, which is about a star as well. 'exploding' scrambles only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering off the right path or route means going wrong.

clue.text: For the star-struck it provides an opening for a good stare, perhaps

definitions.text: For the star-struck it provides an opening

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fans gather at a theatre entrance hoping to gawp at a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GOOD and STARE; 'for a' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans wait at the backstage exit of a theatre to see actors come out after a show.

clue.text: Area of influence for party yes man

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a minion is a servile follower who agrees with everything

explanation.surface: A political party's sycophant extends its reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory under someone's control or rule is their sphere of sway.

clue.text: … one brilliant star

definitions.meaning: an ... counts as one on dice or cards

explanation.surface: A single shining star continues the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the star of 14-across, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The playing card valued at one also names a champion or outstanding player.

clue.text: Nutty biscuits

explanation.surface: Biscuits with nuts in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and the name for thin savoury wafers eaten with cheese.

clue.text: There's a National Trust worker on the hill

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity that owns many hills

explanation.surface: A National Trust employee is stationed up on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hill' is an anthill; worker ants build and tend it. The National Trust is the British heritage charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects live in a colony mound, which is an anthill.

clue.text: Tinker with lifemanship?

definitions.meaning: to tinker is to ..., to work aimlessly at small jobs
Stephen ... wrote the humorous books 'Gamesmanship' and 'Lifemanship'

explanation.surface: Fiddling about with the art of getting one up on people.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition names the author by his book: Stephen Potter coined 'lifemanship'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle about idly at odd jobs, and the surname of the humorist who wrote 'Lifemanship'.

clue.text: Part of kimono billowing reveals sash

indicators.note: part of says only a piece of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A flowing piece of a kimono turns out to be its sash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to the letters straddling 'kimonO BIllowing'; 'reveals' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The wide belt worn round a Japanese robe has its own name.

clue.text: White-collar worker involved in row, perhaps

definitions.text: White-collar worker involved in row, perhaps

parts.words: White-collar worker involved in row, perhaps
parts.note: reads like an office worker in a dispute; really a pupil of a school known for its broad white Eton collar, who might row on the Thames

explanation.surface: An office worker caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College pupils once wore wide white 'Eton collars', and the school is famous for rowing; 'row' looks like a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of the famous English boarding school wore a white collar and might be a rower.

clue.text: Beggar blithe at first and more carefree

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: lighter can mean more light-hearted, less weighed down

explanation.surface: A cheerful vagrant becomes even more relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives B from 'blithe'. 'Beggar' is used in its British sense of a rascal or chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are mildly abusive British terms for a person, a rotter or wretch.

clue.text: Make brief visit for card game with family

parts.note: loo is an old gambling card game
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: Dropping by for a hand of cards with relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone briefly is to pop round.

clue.text: Brighton, say, for repair

definitions.meaning: Brighton is a seaside holiday town on the English south coast
to repair to a place means to go there

explanation.surface: A seaside town chosen for mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' looks like mending, but it means going somewhere, as in 'repair to the bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday town by the sea, and to go or turn to somewhere or something.

clue.text: Hip-coat is altered for a nut

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters before it are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tailored coat is remodelled with a nutty theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges HIPCOAT and IS; 'for' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The green kernel eaten salted or used in ice cream is a nut from a Middle Eastern tree.

clue.text: The jolly unit of heat

parts.note: a Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful measure of warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is slang for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: A British measure of gas energy equal to 100,000 British thermal units.

clue.text: Impressions of specialist in outskirts of Dallas

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside the other
outskirts means the outer parts, so the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a medical specialty

explanation.surface: A doctor's effect on the edges of a Texan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes D and S, the first and last letters of 'Dallas'; 'in' puts ENT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollows pressed into a surface are marks left by an impact.

clue.text: Piercer hired out to make muffin

parts.note: a pike is a long spear for piercing
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A spear is rented out to make a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thick pancake or crumpet, in some regions a kind of teacake.

clue.text: This reptile is around no longer

definitions.text: This reptile is around no longer

parts.words: This reptile is around no longer
parts.note: describes an extinct reptile, a prehistoric creature long gone

explanation.surface: A lizard has died out.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant prehistoric reptiles became extinct some 66 million years ago.

clue.text: Backward talking-bird states intense dislike

indicators.note: backward means the bird's name is written in reverse order

parts.note: mina is a spelling of myna, the Asian starling that mimics speech
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A slow parrot in America provokes hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: MINA is a less common spelling of the myna bird. 'Backward' reverses the bird's name only, not 'states'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or ill will directed at someone is a feeling of strong animosity.
